meta.title: Final policy, two-finger hand — genuine stack
meta.note: Recorded from the last checkpoint of the two-finger run, at the same stiff OSC gains it trained under. 43 episodes rendered, 3 successes, 1 lasting longer than the 10-step boundary below which a success is only a reset that spawned solved — 28 steps, 3.9 mm final error against a 5 mm tolerance.

meta.title: Six genuine stacks from the final policy
meta.note: Last checkpoint of the two-finger carry-shaped run, recorded at the stiff OSC gains it trained under. 51 episodes, 11 successes, 6 of them lasting past the 10-step boundary below which a success is only a reset that spawned solved — 21, 22, 32, 35 and 42 steps, final errors 2.6-4.9 mm against a 5 mm tolerance. Every one ends with the cube at rest (0.0-2 mm/s) and the hand withdrawn 149-176 mm: the success predicate requires neither, so release is measured rather than assumed.

meta.title: Six genuine stacks, earlier checkpoint
meta.note: Cut from a 58-episode rollout by the same success predicate the reward reads. Each ran well past the 10-step boundary below which a success is only a reset that spawned solved: 28, 33, 39 and 51 steps, final errors 4.2-4.8 mm against a 5 mm tolerance. All six end with the cube at rest and the hand withdrawn (154-174 mm away, 0.0-9.9 mm/s).

meta.title: After: a constant closing bias
meta.note: Same family, same null action, one parameter different. Across 64 environments the drop falls to 15 mm, fingertip force rises to 2.58 N, and palm-to-cube SHRINKS from 178 to 174 mm as the fingers draw the cube in.

meta.title: Before: the hand never closes
meta.note: Null action for a whole episode, camera on the cube that is supposed to be held. The fingers stay splayed open beside it. Across 64 environments the cube falls 102 mm to 34 mm and every fingertip reads under 0.01 N against a 0.29 N cube.

meta.title: Close-up camera, derived from the bank geometry
meta.caption: The stored reset banks put the receptive cube at (0.482, 0.012, 0.021) and the insertive at z 0.056, so the camera looks at (0.48, 0.01, 0.045) from 0.42 m at 15 degrees elevation, on the far side of the workspace from the arm base. The cube now subtends ~100 px instead of ~30, and the stack is legible even after the hand withdraws.

meta.title: The scene
meta.caption: Blue cube is the receptive base, spawned kinematic so it cannot be pushed. The red-and-green cube is the one to be placed; its coloured faces are what make the oriented variant's criterion visible. Green quad is the table mat.

meta.title: Placed and released
meta.caption: Near-goal episode 53, 51 steps, final object-to-goal error 4.7 mm against a 5 mm tolerance. The green cube is set square on the blue base and the fingers lift clear: hand 174 mm from the cube at the end, cube moving at 10 mm/s. The success predicate requires none of that -- it tests one distance and would score a cube still held at the goal point identically -- so the release is measured separately and every one of the six genuine successes in this rollout satisfies it.

meta.title: What a pre-solved reset looks like
meta.caption: Near-goal episode 19, scored a success, ran 10 steps. The cube is ALREADY stacked at the first frame -- red-on-green sitting square on the blue base -- and nothing changes for the whole episode. 9 of the 125 stored near-goal reset states (7.2%) spawn inside the 5 mm tolerance like this, which is why the raw success rate cannot be read without splitting by episode length.

meta.title: Null action, 0.05 rad closing bias on every hand joint
meta.caption: The same family and the same zero action, with the constant closing offset. The fingers close on the cube and keep it. A different reset state is drawn at random, so read the pair as illustration -- the measurement is the 64-environment probe: drop 68 mm to 15 mm, fingertip force 0.01 N to 2.58 N.

meta.title: Null action, no grip bias: the fingers never close
meta.caption: One Stable-Grasp episode under the zero action, camera on the cube that is supposed to be held. The green insertive cube sits beside the fingers for all 160 steps while the hand drifts past it. Nothing in the frame is the policy's doing -- the action is identically zero, so this is what the RESET produces.
